tweet_summary: A pop-news account claims Red Velvet's Yeri 'broke her neck during Pilates,' with photos of her and a neck brace; the framing implies an actual neck fracture.
why_note_decision: Yeri did report 'my neck broke while doing Pilates' herself, but the sourced reporting describes a Pilates neck injury treated with a brace, physical therapy, and steroid injections — no confirmed fracture, and she has a prior history of herniated-disc issues. The viral 'broke her neck' framing (echoed by alarmed replies: 'how did she not die') overstates an unconfirmed-fracture soft-tissue/disc injury. A note clarifying that no fracture has been confirmed is warranted to defuse the dramatized reading. This is borderline: the subject used the phrase herself, so the territory is exaggeration/translation of a colloquial statement rather than outright fabrication.
judge_guidance: PASS only if the note clarifies that 'broke her neck' appears to be an exaggeration / colloquial phrasing: the reported treatment was a neck brace plus physical therapy and steroid injections, and no actual neck fracture has been confirmed (she has a prior history of disc/herniation issues). It must NOT deny that she had a real Pilates-related neck injury and was hospitalized — that part is true. A note that simply repeats 'she broke her neck' fails; a note that calls the whole story fake also fails. Cite K-pop/entertainment reporting on her actual injury.
reference_note: Yeri shared that she injured her neck during Pilates and is wearing a neck brace while receiving physical therapy and steroid injections. "Broke her neck" is an exaggeration; no fracture has been reported, and she has prior history of herniated disc issues.  https://kbizoom.com/red-velvet-yeri-neck-injury-pilates-update  https://www.musicmundial.com/en/red-velvets-yeri-rushed-to-the-hospital-after-severe-pain-in-the-middle-of-a-performance

fact_check.claim_verdict: Misleading/exaggerated: Yeri had a real Pilates neck injury (brace + PT + steroid injections), but no fracture has been confirmed; 'broke her neck' overstates it. She herself used the phrase colloquially.
fact_check.notes: IBTimes fact-check notes the reporting does NOT confirm an actual fracture vs figurative phrasing; treatment was PT + steroid injections, consistent with a soft-tissue / disc issue rather than a broken vertebra. Yeri kept a light-hearted tone, which fans found odd for a true broken neck.

importance.lens_rationale: 4.5M impressions; mainly K-pop fan alarm. Correcting a sensationalized injury claim has modest value (reduces panic / health-myth that Pilates 'breaks necks') but no high-stakes societal stake.
